top_choice_rationale: Optical lattice clocks rest on one simple, slightly surprising idea, the magic wavelength that cancels the light shift of the clock levels so that the trap does not disturb the transition it holds. It was realised, taken to the 10^-18 frontier, and reproduced and compared by several independent laboratories, with theory and measurement agreeing closely on the systematic shifts. The two-name allocation (Katori, Ye) is clean and the citation can rest on the lattice clock itself, distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes. P002 is a real, mature achievement, but I defer to colleagues on condensed matter, the 2016 topological prize is a close precedent and the credit is harder to allocate, so I rank it second and above no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; I collaborate closely with 2023 laureate Anne L'Huillier on attosecond physics, but have no documented connection to Katori, Ye, Kane, Mele or Molenkamp.
